title: The text discusses Mozambique's debt service payments from 1995 to 1998, highlighting the increasing amounts owed and the impact of the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (HIPC) initiative. It notes discrepancies in debt service figures provided by the IMF and the government's budget expectations. Additionally, it touches on Shell's operations in the Niger Delta, where community relations have deteriorated despite claims of improved dialogue. The report indicates rising tensions and environmental concerns, particularly regarding Shell's impact on local communities and sacred sites. Overall, the text illustrates the challenges faced by Mozambique in managing its debt and the complexities of corporate-community relations in oil-producing regions.
